exam.q: Staff want to use an AI chatbot to summarize documents containing customers' personal information. What should a Canadian SME confirm first?
opts: That the chatbot is free
That the use fits the purposes people were told, privacy obligations such as PIPEDA, and the vendor's data handling
That the output looks professional
Nothing; summaries are always allowed
exam.why: Privacy laws require personal information to be used for identified purposes with appropriate safeguards, including when third-party tools process it.

exam.q: On a value-effort matrix, e-invoicing scores value 4 and effort 2. Where does it fall and what does that suggest?
opts: Quick win; schedule it early to build momentum
Strategic project; plan over 18 months
Fill-in; do only if spare time exists
Avoid; drop it
exam.why: High value with low effort is a quick win, ideal for the first roadmap horizon.

exam.q: A pilot of digital intake forms has run for five months with no decision because 'results look promising.' What was most likely missing from the pilot plan?
opts: A vendor contract
More tablets
A defined end date and decision rule for scale, adjust or stop
A larger marketing budget
exam.why: Without an end date and decision rule, pilots drift into 'pilot purgatory'.

exam.q: Operators resist new job-tracking tablets because they fear being monitored, even though they understand why the change is happening. Which ADKAR stage is the main barrier?
opts: Awareness
Knowledge
Ability
Desire
exam.why: They understand the reason but do not want the change; addressing concerns and involving them builds desire.

exam.q: Six months after go-live, a benefits register shows re-keying hours above target because two customers still send paper orders. What does this example show?
opts: Benefits registers are unnecessary once a system is live
Tracking benefits reveals fixable adoption gaps that would otherwise go unnoticed
The original target should be removed
The system failed and should be replaced
exam.why: Ongoing benefits tracking surfaces specific causes, such as adoption gaps, so they can be corrected.

figures.title: Three layers of digital transformation
figures.caption: Click each layer, starting at the bottom, to see how each one builds on the one below.

layers.label: Digitization
layers.text: Convert paper and manual records into digital form, such as scanned work orders, electronic timesheets and digital intake forms.

layers.label: Digitalization
layers.text: Use digital tools to improve existing processes, such as barcode scanning to cut picking errors or shared project templates.

layers.label: Transformation
layers.text: Change the operating model itself, such as a customer self-service portal or selling equipment uptime instead of spare parts.

figures.title: Change requests: where the work waits
figures.caption: Watch requests queue at the intake step, then press Fix the bottleneck to see the flow after improvement.

steps.label: Client emails request
steps.text: The request arrives by email, often missing drawings, scope or job details.

steps.label: Intake and logging
steps.text: Staff chase missing information from the client and re-key details into a spreadsheet log and the project system.

steps.label: Engineering review
steps.text: An engineer assesses the change and prepares the technical response.

steps.label: Approval
steps.text: The change is reviewed and approved before work is scheduled.

steps.label: Client notified
steps.text: The client receives the decision and the project record is updated.

config.fix_text: A complete intake form and a single log remove the loops back to the client and the triple data entry, so requests reach engineering ready to work.

figures.title: Digitize the mess vs optimize first
figures.caption: Toggle between the two approaches to see what gets built into the software in each case.

left.title: Automate as-is
points: Six steps and three signatures hard-coded into the workflow
Rules are unclear, so configuration is complex and hard to change

right.title: Eliminate, simplify, standardize, then automate
points: Second approval removed for purchases under $500
One requisition template with required fields
Simple routing rules that are easy to configure and change

figures.title: The DMAIC improvement cycle
figures.caption: Click each phase to see its key question and typical tools.

stages.label: Define
stages.text: What is the problem and who is affected? Use a project charter, SIPOC and voice of the customer.

stages.label: Measure
stages.text: How big is the problem today? Build a data collection plan, a baseline and a process map.

stages.label: Analyze
stages.text: What causes it? Use a fishbone diagram, 5 Whys and a Pareto chart to find the verified root cause.

stages.label: Improve
stages.text: What fixes the root cause? Select solutions, run pilots and add error-proofing.

stages.label: Control
stages.text: How do we keep the gain? Use control charts, standard work and clear ownership of the process.

figures.title: An AI-ready systems foundation
figures.caption: Click each layer from the bottom up to see what an AI-ready architecture rests on.

config.top_label: AI tools that can use your data

layers.label: Systems map
layers.text: List every application, the data it holds, who uses it and whether each connection is integrated, file-based or manual.

layers.label: One system of record
layers.text: Each data type lives in one authoritative system, such as customers in the CRM or ERP, not in both independently.

layers.label: Open APIs, connectors
layers.text: Systems with open APIs and built-in connectors share data without people copying it, starting with manual links.

layers.label: Identity and access
layers.text: Single sign-on and role-based access keep security manageable as the number of systems grows.

layers.label: Controlled data access
layers.text: Clean data is reachable through controlled interfaces, which is what makes adding AI tools straightforward.
